lede: The biggest thing to track this week is Town Council's June 30 meeting, where first reading of Land Use Code amendments tied to Colorado's Wildfire Resiliency Code goes on the table — rules that will shape how development and fire risk are managed in this canyon for a long time. That same night, the Telluride Housing Authority meets on some organizational groundwork worth keeping an eye on. Before that, Thursday's P&Z work session kicks off the formal feedback process on the Shandoka Lot Redevelopment Project, and the Hospital District board sits down for a substantive mill levy discussion.

notable.stake: Mill levy discussion could affect how the hospital district is funded long-term.
Early public shaping of the major Town-owned Shandoka redevelopment before formal review.
First reading of wildfire resiliency land use code changes affecting all future development.
